note: Ground truth for the peer-review-panel calibration fixture. Each flaw is planted in the manuscript on purpose. score_review_panel.py checks a review's text for ANY of a flaw's trigger phrases (case-insensitive substring match) as a coarse, deterministic proxy for 'did the reviewer catch this.' This is a floor check, not a semantic grader -- a review can legitimately catch a flaw while phrasing it in words the fixture doesn't anticipate, which would score as a miss. Treat the number as indicative, not authoritative, and read the actual review text before concluding a tool 'failed' a flaw.

flaws.description: Manuscript claims '97% accuracy across all clients' but the linked evidence record (E001) and claim record (C001) show 97% is a single outlier client's result, with the actual across-client mean at 89.1%.

Manuscript claims to be 'the first to apply differential privacy to federated learning' while its own Related Work section cites two prior differentially-private federated learning papers (Chen et al. 2022; Okafor et al. 2022).

The proposed method is trained for 200 communication rounds while the FedAvg baseline is trained for only 80 rounds -- an unmatched training budget that is a plausible alternative explanation for the accuracy gap, never ruled out.

The causal claim that the improvement 'comes from our aggregation rule directly countering client drift' is hedged with 'results suggest' but no statistical test, ablation, or control isolating the aggregation rule from the round-budget difference is reported -- the hedge does not supply the missing evidence.

'Client drift resilience' is used repeatedly as a load-bearing term (including as the paper's title) but is never operationally defined -- no metric, threshold, or measurement procedure for it is given anywhere in the manuscript.
